title: Live Shop Execution Core
brief: Turn the canonical shop domain into a production execution core for traveler scans, department check-ins, concurrent labor timers, quantity actuals, and live room fanout so the app can operate as the shop's real-time source of truth.

phases.title: Execution Engines + Transport
phases.description: Build the live traveler, labor, quantity, and realtime fanout core that powers shop-floor execution.

units.title: Traveler execution + concurrent labor timer engines
entry_conditions: ULT-MS0 canonical job, traveler, and live-event contracts are available.
Department check-in, task start/stop, and quantity actual rules are documented.
exit_conditions: Traveler scans, department handoffs, task assignment, and concurrent labor sessions flow through dedicated engines.
The execution engines produce analytics-ready events instead of UI-local state.
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)
units.rollback: Remove the new execution engines and restore the seeded UI-only tracker flow.

steps.instruction: Implement traveler progression, duplicate scan detection, department check-in, and quantity actual logic as backend-owned services.
Add concurrent labor timers that support fast mobile start, pause, stop, reassignment, and analytics capture across overlapping tasks.
steps.validation: A single employee can hold multiple active sessions without corrupting traveler or cost state.

deliverables.description: Traveler scan, department handoff, and duplicate-check orchestration.
Multi-task labor timer orchestration for mobile-first shop-floor execution.

units.description: Traveler execution + concurrent labor timer engines — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Shop-floor routes + realtime gateway
entry_conditions: Execution engines expose canonical mutations and snapshots.
The websocket room model for jobs, departments, and employees is defined.
exit_conditions: Dedicated shop-floor routes exist for scan, check-in, task timer, and quantity actual mutations.
Realtime fanout publishes job, department, and employee room updates from one gateway.
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)
units.rollback: Remove the shopFloor route surface and revert consumers to the older ERP-only route bundle.

steps.instruction: Expose HTTP mutations for traveler scan, department check-in, task start or pause or stop, and quantity actual capture.
Fan the resulting events through a realtime gateway so every open job desk and employee device stays synchronized.
steps.validation: Every mutation emits a matching room event with the canonical job or employee identifiers.

deliverables.description: HTTP route surface for scan, check-in, timer, and quantity actual mutations.
Room-based live fanout for job, department, and employee updates.

units.description: Shop-floor routes + realtime gateway — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Dispatcher + analytics contract alignment
entry_conditions: The shop-floor API and realtime gateway are functioning against canonical state.
Actual cost and employee tracking data sources are identified.
exit_conditions: Dispatchers and analytics payloads can access scan, labor, quantity, and route state without bespoke adapters.
Shop execution data is usable by quote variance, cost, and throughput analytics surfaces.
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)
units.rollback: Undo dispatcher wiring and return analytics consumers to previous seeded data paths.

steps.instruction: Update dispatcher surfaces to expose execution-core actions for scan, labor, quantity, and live status lookup.
Align actual-cost and analytics payloads with the new execution contracts so downstream dashboards can consume them directly.
steps.validation: Analytics inputs can distinguish estimated, actual, concurrent, and extra-quantity values per operation.

deliverables.description: Dispatcher extensions for live shop execution actions and room queries.
Actual cost integration with concurrent labor and quantity actual inputs.

units.description: Dispatcher + analytics contract alignment — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

custom_checks: Duplicate scans are rejected or idempotent across HTTP and websocket flows.
Concurrent labor sessions never orphan traveler, employee, or cost state.

phases.title: Forge-Triple Execution Surfaces
phases.description: Package the execution core into operator-facing command surfaces and guard it with hooks and integration tests.

units.title: Shop-floor scan command + execution template
entry_conditions: Execution routes and events are stable enough to expose to operators.
The team wants a repeatable command surface for scans and live status checks.
exit_conditions: A slash-command style doc exists for scan and check-in workflows.
A reusable template captures the canonical execution payloads and event expectations.
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)
units.rollback: Delete the command and template artifacts and rely on raw API docs only.

steps.instruction: Write a shop scan command doc that covers traveler scan, department check-in, live status, and duplicate handling.
Create a forge-triple template that future units can reuse for execution-core prompts, payloads, and room expectations.
steps.validation: The command doc and template reference the same canonical route and event names.

deliverables.description: Slash-command style operator guide for live traveler scanning and check-in.
Forge-triple execution template for shop-floor payloads, live events, and prompts.

units.description: Shop-floor scan command + execution template — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Duplicate-scan guard + integration proof
entry_conditions: The shop-floor transport surface is ready for end-to-end validation.
exit_conditions: A guard detects duplicate or contradictory scan transitions before they corrupt state.
Integration coverage proves scan, timer, and quantity flows emit stable live updates.
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)
units.rollback: Disable the new guard and restore the prior integration suite if false positives block execution.

steps.instruction: Implement a duplicate traveler scan guard that distinguishes safe repeats from invalid state transitions.
Add an integration proof for scan, timer, and quantity flows with websocket fanout and analytics payload assertions.
steps.validation: The integration suite proves idempotent duplicate handling and live update propagation.

deliverables.description: Hook-style duplicate and contradiction guard for traveler scan transitions.
Integration proof for traveler scan, labor timer, and quantity actual live flows.

units.description: Duplicate-scan guard + integration proof — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

custom_checks: Every operator-facing command references a real route and event contract.
Integration coverage proves duplicate-scan protection and live fanout.

tool_map.purpose: Implement engines, routes, commands, and tests
Check coverage and canonical contract completeness
Run forge-triple review on the guard and integration proof

existing_leverage.usage: Timer semantics and employee clock state
Downstream cost rollups and actual-versus-estimate analysis
Dispatch desk consumer of live execution state
